record_policy: Architecture selections requested on 2026-10-25 remain selected_for_validation; accepted records identify owner-confirmed tradeoffs. Neither status proves implementation or explicit owner selection of every technology. Supersede material decisions with rationale; preserve historical records after implementation depends on them.

decisions.decision: Use a local-first modular monolith with explicit external ports and feature-oriented module internals.
decisions.reason: Bound local change and AI context while avoiding premature deployment, networking and distributed consistency costs.
decisions.cost: Boundaries require enforcement; a single process shares some failure and resource limits.
decisions.revisit_when: Measured isolation, independent deployment or multi-user requirements cannot be met with a bounded worker/adapter.
decisions.reversal: Extract a demonstrated boundary behind its existing port; migrate ownership explicitly rather than exposing internal tables.

decisions.decision: Separate observations, interpretations, owner intent, plans and verification; render maps as projections.
decisions.reason: A model update or UI rewrite must not overwrite user decisions or redefine source facts.
alternatives: One mutable knowledge graph for every concept
Model conversation history as the only memory
decisions.cost: Explicit provenance, mapping and partial/stale states add implementation work.
decisions.revisit_when: A concrete domain distinction has no independent lifecycle or change behavior; simplify only without losing authority/provenance separation.
decisions.reversal: Change internal representation through versioned export/migration; preserve record identities and provenance.

decisions.decision: Use current-state records plus targeted revision/audit history, and rebuildable projections; do not event-source the entire application.
decisions.reason: Support revisable ideas and historical evidence without making every future change depend on replaying all historical events.
decisions.cost: Each revisioned aggregate needs explicit history semantics and migration rules; generic time travel is not promised.
decisions.revisit_when: A specific aggregate demonstrably needs temporal reconstruction that targeted revisions cannot support.
decisions.reversal: Introduce event history for that aggregate through an adapter; preserve supported exports and current-state readers.

decisions.decision: Use C#/.NET for product logic, Avalonia for a desktop-rendered UI and SQLite for local state; pin supported versions at bootstrap.
decisions.reason: A common typed language across desktop, core and collectors reduces coordination surfaces; the desktop renderer and storage remain replaceable.
decisions.cost: Custom graph interactions, parser ecosystem coverage, platform accessibility and packaging require real prototypes; language choice alone does not ensure maintainability.
decisions.revisit_when: The first graph/packaging/analyzer spike fails measured requirements or verified target-platform constraints make the stack unsuitable.
decisions.reversal: Replace the failing UI or analyzer adapter first. A full language rewrite preserves exported data and behavioral fixtures but still has substantial cost.

decisions.decision: Use one local canonical writer, SQLite transactions and a separate disposable artifact/cache boundary.
decisions.reason: Preserve owner records atomically with minimal operations; avoid cross-OS database sharing and accidental coupling to graph/search engines.
alternatives: Shared live JSON files as primary storage
decisions.cost: Write throughput is bounded; migrations, artifact consistency, export and restore still need deliberate implementation.
decisions.revisit_when: Measured write contention or confirmed collaborative multi-user operation exceeds local single-writer requirements.
decisions.reversal: Keep owner repository ports and portable exports, migrate through verified snapshots and designate one writer during cutover.

decisions.decision: Treat fast/deep AI as replaceable capability profiles with typed evidence-grounded output, not as authorities or separate permanent agent personalities.
decisions.reason: Provider quality, price and availability will change; product memory and permission enforcement must survive those changes.
alternatives: Bind workflows to specific model names
Let a general autonomous agent own all state
Make AI inference mandatory for basic navigation
decisions.cost: Routing, evaluations, schema validation and evidence retrieval require explicit engineering; smaller models may not pass a task's quality bar.
decisions.revisit_when: Representative evaluations show one model is simpler/better or a new role has a distinct measurable requirement.
decisions.reversal: Change profile mapping and provider adapter; preserve accepted result snapshots, permissions and input provenance.

decisions.decision: Use staged replacement behind tested contracts, with one active writer and temporary compatibility paths.
decisions.reason: Reduce the blast radius of incorrect decisions while keeping the old behavior available during evidence gathering.
decisions.cost: Temporary duplication and migration fixtures are necessary; destructive schema changes and remote effects still have real reversal cost.
decisions.revisit_when: An existing interface is itself wrong; version or replace the boundary instead of preserving a bad abstraction indefinitely.
decisions.reversal: Use a tested compatible switchback or explicit forward repair; remove transitional code after its recorded retirement condition.

decisions.decision: Prioritize inexpensive recurring changes and bounded failed experiments; make major migrations and rewrites controlled rather than promising every change is cheap.
decisions.reason: The owner accepted this tradeoff on 2026-10-25. Speculative interfaces and perpetual compatibility add ongoing cost even when the anticipated change never occurs.
alternatives: Prebuild flexibility for every possible change
decisions.cost: An unexpected or fundamental change may still require substantial redesign and migration; that cost alone does not invalidate the architecture.
decisions.revisit_when: Actual recurring changes cross too many owners, failed experiments leave persistent burden, or a new confirmed requirement changes the expected costs.
decisions.reversal: Revise only the demonstrated boundary and preserve owner records and relevant behavior fixtures. Remove superseded abstractions and temporary compatibility paths.
